title: Do not override canonical per-subscription recurring topology with an unsupported global cap
inherited_objective: Assess MCP/worker behavior together with current WIP and recent history, including whether the ten scheduled workers (five per subscription) and their recovery/tool behavior look normal; keep the manual/on-demand swarm separate.
live_state: Canonical topology defines five scheduled recurring workers in S1 and five in S2, ten scheduled workers total.
Manual/on-demand swarm is a separate population and does not count against those ten scheduled workers.
Current S1 scheduler shows five enabled scheduled workers: Hazel, Larch, Maple, Pine, and Alder.
Current local slot registry is stale/misaligned for S1: four bindings with Hazel, Cypress, Larch, and Sequoia, S1/5 unbound.
Fleet-watch therefore requires exact live scheduler confirmation before any same-partition recovery mutation.
protected_state: Do not rewrite the intended ten scheduled workers into a global five-worker cap.
Do not mix manual/on-demand swarm counts into the scheduled ten-worker fleet.
Do not promote the mutable slot-binding registry into live scheduler truth.
Do not use a corrective trigger itself as scheduler-mutation authority.
hard_exclusions: Do not invent a max-five-total constraint absent current user direction.
Do not call the canonical S1=5 plus S2=5 topology wrong on that invented basis.
Do not re-enable a candidate without the required exact live scheduler probe.

failure_candidate.action: Treat five as a global scheduled-worker maximum, count manual swarm together with scheduled workers, or diagnose stale registry membership as if it were the live scheduler fleet.

success_candidate.action: Preserve ten scheduled workers total (five per subscription), keep manual swarm separate, read live scheduler state for actual enabled membership, and use registry/fleet-watch only as guarded recovery evidence reconciled against that scheduler.

discriminating_evidence: Whether scheduled fleet is stated as S1 five plus S2 five, ten total.
Whether manual/on-demand swarm is kept separate.
Whether live scheduler membership outranks stale/misaligned slot-binding projection for enabled-state claims.
Whether recovery remains gated by exact live scheduler confirmation.
completion_condition: The corrected response states 10 scheduled workers total, keeps manual swarm separate, reports the live S1 scheduler as five enabled workers, and identifies the stale S1 slot registry as a coordination/attribution drift rather than a scheduler-capacity failure.

memory_candidate.title: Scheduled worker fleet is 5 per subscription, 10 total; manual swarm is separate
memory_candidate.text: The recurring scheduled fleet consists of five workers in S1 and five in S2, ten scheduled workers total. Manual/on-demand swarm is separate. For actual enabled membership use the owning live scheduler; slot registry/fleet-watch is mutable coordination/recovery evidence and must be reconciled against exact scheduler state before mutation.
memory_candidate.interpretation: The failure was an unsupported global-cap assumption plus authority selection: scheduler truth was conflated with slot-registry projection. No new shared rule is required.
memory_candidate.confidence_reason: Direct user correction plus canonical topology, live slot-registry output, and fresh S1 fleet-watch all agree on the five-per-partition model and guarded peer recovery semantics.

analysis.failure_boundary: The preceding status synthesis invented a global max-five recurring-worker constraint and used it to label the correct scheduled topology as wrong. It also failed to distinguish the live scheduler fleet from the mutable local slot-binding registry and from the separate manual/on-demand swarm.
analysis.user_needed: A current MCP/worker/WIP/history assessment that preserves the actual scheduled topology: five scheduled workers per subscription, ten scheduled workers total, maintained through guarded same-partition recovery when workers/tool routes drop; manual/on-demand swarm is separate.
analysis.assistant_did: It found the ten-slot contract but overrode it with an unsupported max-five-total assumption. After that, it treated a stale/misaligned slot-binding projection as if it described the actual scheduled fleet instead of checking the live scheduler first.
analysis.first_supported_divergence: The answer stated that ten scheduled slots were inconsistent with the user's target. Fresh evidence now shows the canonical model is five scheduled workers per subscription, the live S1 scheduler currently has five enabled workers, while the local S1 slot registry is stale/misaligned and therefore must not be promoted into scheduler truth.

governing_guidance.source: RULES.md recurring-fleet topology and liveness are separate dimensions
swarm_topology canonical contract: S1 five plus S2 five

analysis.correct_counterfactual: Preserve the canonical model: five scheduled workers in S1 plus five scheduled workers in S2, ten scheduled workers total; manual/on-demand swarm is separate. For actual fleet state, read the owning scheduler. Use the slot registry/fleet-watch as recovery coordination evidence only and reconcile it against exact live scheduler state before any re-enable.
analysis.repaired_result: Corrected current status: the intended fleet is 10 scheduled workers total, 5 per subscription, with manual/on-demand swarm separate. In the S1 scheduler visible here, Hazel, Larch, Maple, Pine, and Alder are all enabled, so S1 currently has its full five scheduled workers enabled. The local slot registry is stale/misaligned: it reports only four S1 bindings and names Hazel, Cypress, Larch, and Sequoia, leaving S1/5 unbound. Therefore the current issue is registry/fleet-watch attribution drift, not missing S1 scheduler capacity. S2 scheduler enabled state remains outside this S1 scheduler view.

behavior_contract_review.reason: Existing authority-selection and topology/liveness rules already cover the failure; no new shared rule is justified.

analysis.unresolved_uncertainty: Exact S2 scheduler enabled state is not visible from this S1 scheduler surface. The local slot registry currently disagrees with live S1 scheduler membership and should not be used as scheduler truth until reconciled.
